Has anyone been able to figure out how to add a new user to a Group Operational Resource plan? It's referenced in the Rome release notes but the links go to the information for allowing management of operational resource plans in the allocation workbench. Is there an admin setting? ‎04-27-2022 03:00 PM. First of all, two configuration steps are required to create/manage operational resource plans (RPLNs) from the resource allocation workbench (RAW). 1. Enable the system property (as a system admin). ’ Create and manage operational resource plans from the resource allocation workbench’. 2. Select ’Operational Plans’ option from RAW configuration (as a resource manager). Now as a resource manager (RM), one can add new resources to a completely confirmed / allocated operational RPLN provided it is created using %capacity and not by hours. A res grp has 3 resources and all of them have 176 hours capacity from Jun - Sep. Now create a group Operational RPLN (Jun – Aug) for 10% capacity. Then confirm / allocate this operational RPLN. As a result, resource finder will display the reduced capacity & availability and increased allocations. At this point, the planned and allocated hours on the allocated RPLN will be same. Now a new member is added to this group. To add this user to the (above created) allocated operational RPLN, select this user from the resource finder and allocate. On adding the resource to the RPLN, percent capacity defined on the operational RPLN (in this case 10%) will be allocated to the new user. results.title: Accounting for Contingencies and Provisions
results.content: # Accounting for Contingencies and Provisions. The proper accounting treatment for contingencies and provisions requires careful evaluation of probability, estimation of potential outflows, and transparent disclosure. * **Contingency:** An existing condition, situation, or set of circumstances involving uncertainty about a possible gain or loss that will ultimately be resolved by a future event. * **Provision:** A liability of uncertain timing or amount, recognized when there is a present obligation as a result of a past event, it is probable that an outflow of resources will be required, and the amount can be reasonably estimated. US GAAP primarily uses “contingency” for both gains and losses, while IFRS distinguishes between “contingent liabilities” (possible obligations) and “provisions” (probable obligations). **Under US GAAP (ASC 450):**A loss contingency is recognized as an accrual if:. 1. It is probable that a liability has been incurred at the date of the financial statements, and. **Under IFRS (IAS 37):**A provision is recognized if:. * It is probable (more likely than not) that an outflow will be required, and. If the likelihood is possible but not probable, the obligation is disclosed as a contingent liability. Provisions must be measured at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the present obligation at the balance sheet date. Discounting to present value is required under IFRS when the effect is material; US GAAP generally prohibits discounting except for specific obligations (e.g., asset retirement). ### **Examples of Common Provisions and Contingencies**. * **Litigation:** Recognize a provision when settlement is probable and the amount can be estimated. * **Warranty obligations:** Recognize an accrual based on estimated costs to fulfill warranties on products sold. * **Environmental liabilities:** Estimate remediation costs for contamination or asset retirement. A company estimates $50,000 in probable warranty costs for products sold during the year. Comprehensive disclosure is required for all material contingencies and provisions, including:. * Reconciliation of provision balances (IFRS). ### **Contingent Gains**. Contingent gains are **not** recognized in the financial statements under either US GAAP or IFRS. * **US GAAP:** ASC 450 – Contingencies. * **IFRS:** IAS 37 – Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets. ## **Summary Table: Provisions and Contingencies**.
